title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Attacks around Hormuz have reached the UAE's own anchorages: a bulk carrier at anchor off Khor Fakkan was hit, and ten tankers were struck in a single week. Traffic through the strait fell by more than 40% in the past week, while Amazon's White Friday sale runs to Sunday and keeps UAE parcel demand high.

gauges.label: Ships crossing Hormuz, 17–23 Nov vs 1–7 Nov
gauges.note: 125 crossings against 226; 125–140 a day before the war (Marine Traffic via Al Jazeera)

gauges.label: Ships waiting at anchor east of the strait
gauges.note: As of 22 Nov; US-escorted transits averaged 38 a day on 19–21 Nov (JMIC via gCaptain)

gauges.note: IMO tally as of 23 Nov, with 25 seafarers killed (gCaptain)

gauges.note: From about $2,000 before the disruption (DP World GCC CEO, Seatrade Maritime)

gauges.note: Hit by Houthi missile attacks since early October (WorldACD via STAT Times)

gauges.note: Down from yesterday's $90.55; it passed $120 at one point in the war (Al Jazeera)

stories.headline: Bulk carrier hit at anchor off Khor Fakkan; Iran adds tugboats to its blacklist
body: UKMTO reported attacks on three tankers and a bulk carrier on 22 November. The bulk carrier was at anchor off Khor Fakkan when an unidentified projectile caused a fire on board. No one was hurt. That brings reported tanker strikes to 10 in one week.
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority added 26 tugboats to its list of non-compliant vessels, which may now hold about 266 ships. JMIC rates the threat as severe.
stories.soWhat: New: the risk is now inside UAE east-coast anchorages, where our import boxes wait. Tell sea-import customers that Khor Fakkan dwell carries risk as well as delay.

stories.headline: Hormuz traffic down more than 40% in a week
body: Marine Traffic data show 226 vessels entered or left the Gulf on 1–7 November, but only 125 crossed on 17–23 November. Before the war, 125 to 140 ships passed every day.
Iran says it will "definitely not tolerate" the US naval blockade. Brent crude was at $88.35 a barrel.
stories.soWhat: Fewer ships means fewer slots and longer waits into the Gulf. Expect sea-freight rates to stay high and quote validity to stay short.

stories.headline: Saudi air cargo down a third since Houthi attacks began
body: WorldACD says air cargo to and from Saudi Arabia has been hit by Houthi missile attacks since the week of 5 October. Chargeable weight was down 33% against week 40 in its latest week.
The same data show Dubai air rates to Europe and the US more than 80% above last year.
stories.soWhat: Saudi air is shrinking, not just delayed. Road express from the UAE to Saudi is the product to push, not a stopgap.

stories.headline: Amazon's White Friday runs to 30 November after a strong Singles' Day
body: Amazon UAE's White Friday sale runs for 12 days, from 19 to 30 November. UAE orders rose 39% during Singles' Day, and GMV rose 30%, according to Udora and Admitad.
NielsenIQ says online sales of technology and durables in the UAE grew 18.3%.
stories.soWhat: Peak volumes run through Sunday and returns follow in December. Keep extra courier capacity and plan a returns push.

stories.headline: Talabat raises its 2026 outlook, but GCC growth is slower
body: Talabat's Q3 GMV rose 17% to $3 billion and revenue rose 18% to $1.2 billion. It raised full-year guidance for the second time this year.
GMV grew 43% in Egypt, Jordan and Iraq but only 9% in the GCC markets, including the UAE.
stories.soWhat: UAE food and quick-commerce growth is slowing. Sell cost and reliability to delivery platforms, not just extra capacity.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Revised demand surcharges from Europe and the Americas
body: FedEx revised its Middle East demand surcharge on shipments from Europe and US/LAC/Canada from 16 November, until further notice. Other lanes are unchanged.

For Saudi Arabia, imports from the US, Canada, LAC and Europe now carry SAR 12.4 per kg, and exports to the US and Canada SAR 5.8 per kg. GCC lanes carry SAR 2.1 per kg. The minimum is SAR 3.7 per shipment.
competitors.soWhat: FedEx is passing the cost of inbound Europe and US capacity to shippers. Check our import surcharge against these levels before matching or undercutting.

competitors.name: DP World
competitors.headline: Runs 3,000 trucks on the east-coast corridor; 1 million TEU moved
body: DP World GCC CEO Ahmad Yousef Al-Hassan says the company has moved over 1 million TEU between the east coast and the UAE by road and rail since March. It went "from zero to today, 3,000 trucks" that it manages and operates.
He said China to Dubai container rates rose from about $2,000 to $10,000–12,000, and that Jebel Ali calls could take one to three months to recover after Hormuz reopens.
competitors.soWhat: The port operator is now a large trucker on our drayage lane. Sell what DP World does not: customs, last mile and door delivery from the same booking.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: CEO expects rates to stay high for 6 to 12 months after peace
body: Group CEO Amadou Diallo said freight rates would normalise six to 12 months after peace returns. Aramex is aiming for double-digit revenue growth in 2026 and 2027.
Recent growth came from multimodal routes through Turkish ports and gateways such as Sohar, Salalah and Jeddah.
competitors.soWhat: Our own view supports pricing for a long high-rate period. Contracts signed now should not assume a fast fall in rates.

opportunities.title: Oman gateways
opportunities.text: Hormuz crossings fell by more than 40% and the Khor Fakkan anchorage was hit. Sohar and Salalah routes, which already drive our growth, are the safer gate.

opportunities.title: White Friday peak and returns
opportunities.text: Amazon's sale runs to 30 November after a 39% jump in Singles' Day orders. Offer sellers peak capacity now and a returns service for December.

opportunities.title: UAE–Saudi road express
opportunities.text: Saudi air cargo is down 33%. Road is the steady option for UAE shippers selling into the Kingdom.

opportunities.title: Inbound import pricing
opportunities.text: FedEx charges SAR 12.4 per kg on inbound Europe and US. There is room to price our import express at market level.

opportunities.title: Door-to-door on the east coast
opportunities.text: DP World trucks port to port. We can win customers who want one booking from berth to door.

watchouts.title: UAE anchorages in range
watchouts.text: A bulk carrier was hit at anchor off Khor Fakkan. Boxes waiting there carry risk as well as delay.

watchouts.title: Tugs on Iran's blacklist
watchouts.text: 26 tugboats were added to Iran's non-compliant list. Port services in the strait may slow further.

watchouts.title: 218 ships waiting
watchouts.text: Ships are queuing east of the strait. Delivery promises on sea imports need extra time.

watchouts.title: DP World in trucking
watchouts.text: With 3,000 trucks, DP World can bundle drayage with port handling and squeeze our freight margin.

watchouts.title: Slower GCC delivery growth
watchouts.text: Talabat's GCC GMV grew 9% against 43% outside the GCC. Platform clients will push harder on price.

moves.title: Add a risk note to east-coast sea quotes
moves.text: Update sea-import quotes via Khor Fakkan and Fujairah to cover longer waits and war-risk charges after the anchorage strike.

moves.title: Offer an Oman gateway to key importers
moves.text: Call the top sea-import accounts this week with a Sohar or Salalah plus road option into the UAE.

moves.title: Benchmark import surcharges against FedEx
moves.text: Compare our Europe and US inbound surcharge with FedEx's SAR 12.4 per kg and adjust where we are below market.

moves.title: Hold peak capacity through Sunday
moves.text: Keep extra riders and sorting shifts until Amazon's White Friday ends on 30 November, and offer sellers a December returns rate.

moves.title: Pitch berth-to-door against DP World
moves.text: Package drayage, customs and last mile as one price for customers using the east-coast corridor.

moves.title: Push road express into Saudi
moves.text: Brief UAE e-commerce sellers that Saudi air cargo is down a third and move their volume to road express.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
